title: Risk-sensitivity-led Onboarding Playbook and Conditional Pricing Credits
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background: Large enterprise and mid-market customers are delaying buy decisions due to opaque vendor risk workflows and one-size-fits-all SOC2 insurance add-ons. This initiative designs a risk-sensitivity-led onboarding playbook that dynamically surfaces a minimal evidence path for low-risk vendors and conditional pricing credits for customers who adopt automated evidence flows. The intent is to reduce friction, lower procurement lead time, and test whether conditional credits increase conversion and reduce average negotiated discounts.

Goals: 1) Build a documented onboarding playbook that maps risk tiers to a tailored SOC2 evidence bundle and optional attestations. 2) Implement a conditional pricing credit model that auto-applies a tiered credit when vendors complete an automated evidence flow in the vendor portal. 3) Run a 12-week pricing experiment with 50 procurement conversations to validate lift in conversion and reduction in time-to-first-contract.

Success metrics: 1) Reduction in average vendor onboarding lead time from opportunity to contract signature by 30% (baseline measured in Q3). 2) Increase in closed-won rate for SMB and mid-market procurement opportunities by 12% within experiment cohort. 3) At least 40% of eligible vendors complete automated evidence flow and receive credits; net revenue impact neutral or positive over 6 months.

Scope: Includes playbook authoring, vendor portal changes (evidence flow + opt-in credit checkbox), billing adjustments for credits, legal contract addendum templates for conditional credits, and dashboards to measure funnel metrics. Excludes on-prem provisioned packaging and manual contract negotiations for enterprise bespoke terms (handled by Sales Ops).

Out of scope: New insurance procurement, changes to existing SOC2 attestations beyond recommended bundles, and Guaranteed SLAs for credit eligibility beyond experiment period.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published to Confluence with mapping of at least 3 risk tiers and corresponding evidence bundles
Vendor portal UI changes deployed to staging with automated evidence flow and opt-in credit checkbox
Billing system can apply credits conditionally (test invoice generation shows credit applied)
Legal has approved a short addendum template that references the credit experiment
Experiment dashboard surfaces enrollment, completion rate, time-to-contract, and win-rate by cohort
milestones: 2025-11-15: Draft playbook and evidence schemas (PM + Security)
2025-11-30: Vendor portal design prototype and engineering scoping (DES + ENG)
2025-12-12: Billing and legal integration plan sign-off
open_questions: What constitutes sufficient automated evidence to qualify for the credit (SOC2 artifact subset or self-attestation)?
Is the credit refundable if post-contract audit uncovers missing evidence?
How do we communicate the experiment and credit to procurement stakeholders without creating expectations for permanent discounts?
Should credits be applied upfront as invoice credit or as a rebate after validation?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales may overpromise credits causing margin erosion. Mitigation: Clear guardrails + enable Sales Ops to approve exceptions.
Risk: Legal/regulatory concerns around offering conditional credits tied to security attestations. Mitigation: Short addendum reviewed by Legal and Security with expiration clause for experiment.
Risk: Fraudulent evidence submissions. Mitigation: Automated heuristics + manual spot checks by Security & Trust team.
Risk: Engineering scope creep adds delays. Mitigation: MVP portal with manual fallthrough and feature flags for rollout.
